claims.text: The three core artifacts describe one and the same trip: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-00103, the trace runs from 08:07:20 to 08:36:20 and the trip_record's started_at/ended_at are 08:07:20/08:36:20, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on matching identifiers and timestamps across the bundle.

The deviation is established on the figure POL-RD-01 says governs: the gps_trace polyline is 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km and 36.34%, which clears both statutory gates (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). trip_record.actual_distance_km (11.2 km) is only the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be used for the threshold test, so the trace figure is cited here and the finding is safe.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, so the excess stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration: 175 fixes at the expected 10-second sample_interval_sec, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array and max_gap_sec of 0.0 mean none of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires. The rider's profile also carries deviation_claims_60d 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0, so the POL-RD-08 proviso that would demand corroboration beyond the trace is not engaged and may not be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

The LTA closure ADV-20260714-031 on Braddell Road (active 05:30-12:00, overlapping the 08:07-08:36 trip window, shortest lawful alternative 10.6 km) is the reason the driver left the arterials, and the rider does not seek the distance and time charges for that. But the closure does not pay for the rider's gantries: under POL-RD-09(2), where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand but off-route ERP is still refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at SGD 12.00 per trip, because the rider did not cause the closure either.

The whole SGD 4.00 of tolls_erp is due back: both itemised CTE gantry lines are flagged on_optimal_route false — SGD 3.00 (CTE, Braddell Rd towards City, 08:14:06) and SGD 1.00 (CTE, Moulmein Rd towards City, 08:19:41) — while the optimal route the rider booked carries no gantry at all, optimal_route_erp_sgd being 0.00 on the routing-engine-v3.2 description 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. The refund is well inside the SGD 12.00 cap, and because the rider filed and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, the correction is a PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03 rather than a state in which the rider keeps paying for a crossing she never asked for.

The CTE diversion was the driver's decision, not a rider instruction, so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund. The only message naming the diversion is the driver's own 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' sent at 08:12:30; the rider's 'ok' at 08:12:58 is an acknowledgement of a choice already announced, not an instruction. POL-RD-04 requires the instruction to come from the rider and to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on, and the waypoint_hint field is null on both messages — so the clause's corroboration test is undecidable on this record, the clause is unavailable, and the excess cannot be treated as rider-caused.

The ERP figure must be refunded once and once only: under POL-RD-09(1) a POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends off-route ERP, because the recomputed fare includes only gantries on the optimal route, so the SGD 4.00 must never be added on top of a POL-RD-02 figure. On either limb the rider's recovery is the same money — the tolls she was billed for a corridor she did not choose.

If the judge declines to treat the closure as fully exonerating, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic still lands in the rider's favour and should be run against the closure-adjusted optimal: charged_total is 25.12; recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.18 + 0.28 x 28.6) x 1.00 surge from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route = 20.993, using the adjusted optimal of 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km and its duration of 21 x (11.18/8.2) = 28.6 min because amended_optimal_duration_min is null; the raw difference of 4.127 is rounded UP to SGD 4.15. That is the floor on the rider's recovery, not an amount to be added to the ERP correction.

claims.text: The booked optimal route ('Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials') runs straight through the stretch of Braddell Road that an LTA DataMall HIGH-severity closure shut from 05:30 to 12:00 on the trip date, and the trace leaves that corridor at the closure and goes another way. Under POL-RD-03 the whole of the measured excess is therefore exonerated: justified_excess = min(measured 2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 km shortest lawful alternative - 8.2 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km = 4.12 km), and the measured figure is the lesser of the two. Nothing is left over to refund on distance.

Every limb of POL-RD-03 is satisfied on the face of the artifacts. (a) The advisory names 'Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd', a road the trip_record's own optimal route uses. (b) Its 05:30-12:00 window covers the 08:07-08:36 trace window with far more than the 15-minute buffer POL-RD-03 allows. (c) The GPS pre-pass records that the turn-off at the Lorong 1 Toa Payoh slip falls inside the advisory geometry, before the affected segment, and both the driven route and the optimal route terminate at the same booked dropoff.

Once the exonerated 2.98 km comes out, the excess remaining for the threshold test is 0 km against the closure-adjusted optimal. That fails both POL-RD-01 gates - it is not greater than 20% of optimal (1.64 km) and not greater than 0.8 km absolute - so no deviation survives and there is no POL-RD-02 recomputation of distance or time charges to run. The rider's distance and time lines stand.

The route actually driven is the diversion the authority itself signed, not a driver preference: the advisory's description reads 'Diversion via Lorong 1 Toa Payoh or CTE', and the chat log shows the driver announcing at 08:12:30 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' with the rider replying 'ok' at 08:12:58. The alternative the driver would have had to invent was signed by the road authority, and the extra 2.98 km over the booked optimal is within the 4.12 km cap that POL-RD-03 sets on it.

CONCESSION ON THE ERP. The fare ledger bills two CTE gantries - 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' at S$3.00 and 'CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City)' at S$1.00 - both flagged on_optimal_route false, against an optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00. Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event, POL-RD-09(2) requires that S$4.00 of off-route ERP be refunded as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at S$12.00, while the distance and time charges stand because the driver was not at fault. The driver does not resist that S$4.00 correction and argues only that it is the ceiling of the rider's recovery, not a floor.

The two ERP lines are not billing-integrity defects under POL-RD-09(4). The driver announced the CTE routing in the in-app channel before the gantries were crossed at 08:14:06 and 08:19:41, and the ledger itemises them gantry-by-gantry at metered cost; this is a pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(2), not a phantom charge, and no billing-integrity referral is warranted.

The deviation here is not MATERIAL and no POL-RD-06 uplift is available to the rider: 2.98 km and 36.6% sit below the 8.0 km and 50% marks that POL-RD-01 sets for materiality. Even if the profile were consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 553, which establishes no repeat pattern and licenses neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a conduct referral.

Under POL-RD-08 the burden shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause rather than make a general assertion that traffic was bad. The driver discharges it: the LTA closure advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01, read with POL-RD-03, is a named artifact and a named clause, and it covers this trip's window and this trip's corridor. That is the whole of the driver's exculpatory case.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the GPS trace for TRP-00103 is 11.18 km against the booked optimal route of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km or 36.3%. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a deviation is established — but it is not a MATERIAL deviation, since it is below the 8.0 km and 50% marks.

The LTA DataMall closure on Braddell Road (active 05:30–12:00 on the trip date) names a road the optimal route uses, covers the 08:07–08:36 trace window with far more than the 15-minute buffer, and the driver left the corridor before the affected stretch and rejoined it after. Under POL-RD-03 the whole measured excess falls within the exoneration cap of 1.30 x (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km, since 2.98 km is the lesser figure. The excess is therefore fully exonerated, nothing remains to refund on distance, and the distance and time charges stand.

The ERP is a separate line. The route the rider booked carries no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00), yet the fare ledger bills two CTE gantries — S$3.00 and S$1.00, both flagged on_optimal_route false. Because the detour is excused as an external event, POL-RD-09(2) refunds off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at S$12.00. S$4.00 is due. Under POL-RD-09(1) this S$4.00 is never added on top of a distance refund — and there is no distance refund here — so it is the whole of the rider's recovery.

On evidence handling: the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (175 fixes at the expected 10-second interval, coverage_pct 100.0, empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0), so none of the POL-RD-07 limbs fires and no independent corroboration was required. Every artifact carried weight_multiplier 1.0, so no disclosure or discount applied. Both gantry lines correspond to fixes on the trace, so they are genuine pass-through charges and not phantom lines; no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises, and no POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral arises because the driver shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 553 completed trips). No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 is present.

Outcome: the rider's claim is partly upheld. S$4.00 of the disputed amount is refunded; the balance of the fare stands.
